title: Anyone can put pen to paper. It doesn't make them an author.
author: DeepFriedDonkeyDick
selftext:
Anyone can pick up a brush. It doesn't make them a painter. Yada yada and so forth. All these arguments on here "Look at my 1 prompt masterpiece, why aren't you all clapping??" and the "Ai slop this, antis ate my first born that." 

Ai is a TOOL like some of you have already stated. And succinctly, it comes down to the tool being widespread, but a game dev/ artist you are not just because you have access to the tool.  
  
At least one that has mastery of the basic concepts of what makes a good game good, not just for you, but for others around you as well. That takes somethings Ai can't one prompt for you; Experience. Understanding. Learnability. Getting your own head outta your asshole every once and a while and sniffing fresh air.

That's not to say that the dozens of you making games just for you and you circle of people aren't valid either. I guess the big stink is from the many people wanting some sort of validation for their slop. 

THIS SAME THING HAPPENED WITH WHEN GENERATIVE IMAGES WERE FIRST BECOMING VIABLE 2 YEARS AGO! We all got the memories of brain dead gold fish.   
  
History repeats.   
Tale as old as time.  
Song as old as rhyme.  
Beauty and the beast.

comments.author: wewerecreaturres
comments.body: So a game that isn’t good for everyone isn’t a real game?

comments.author: i_rate_slop
comments.body:
weird gatekeep

Anybody working on a game, zero shot slop or not, is a game developer. They’re just shit at it.

I’ll take zero shot tech demos over 99% of what’s on itch

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body: Well, I mean everyone is what they want to be, however others do not need to agree on that. Like because I can make scrambled eggs am I a chef? Sure in my perspective I maybe a chef, others may disagree.

replies.author: SpiritualShallot3
replies.body: Chef does denote a professional title in its definition, developer is a broad generic term.

replies.author: Exhales_Deeply
replies.body:
would you, tho?  
like, would you pay 2 bucks for a game on itch or 2 bucks for a one-shot minecraft clone?

be real

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body:
In a lot of cases yes! Not all, of course.

I’d rather experience the 99th water simulation with 10,000 seagulls on screen than a broken platformer or literally any visual novel.

But don’t take my comment too literally :). I just wanted to express that if those shit games on itch are by game developers, so are these. They’re both just really bad at what they do because of a lack of experience.

replies.author: Exhales_Deeply
replies.body:
unfortunately what's going to go away is an important cycle of working really hard to make something you like > finding out its considered shit to most people > working really hard to make something better

primarily because of the volume

but i see your point and i don't disagree, this is a sub that encompasses the entire spectrum of gamedesign from an hour-one novice to an industry vet with a bajillion shipped titles

replies.author: TopTippityTop
replies.body:
Lol... No, not really. A game developer is someone who de votes their life to development.

A chef isn't anyone who cooks. It's a profession and choice of career. You can still enjoy cooking, even cook quite well, and not be a chef. Same with game development.

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body:
I can get behind not granting someone the title of game developer until they release something for distribution. 

Not sure I agree with this notion of devoting your life to it. Plenty of popular games start as side projects.

comments.author: ViennettaLurker
comments.body:
I'd say using a brush makes you a painter. And putting pen to paper an author. If that is your intent.

That doesn't make it *good* though.

There always seems to be this odd hole in the "what is art?" conversation, where people don't really entertain the idea that art can be bad. Or not compelling. Or not compelling to you personally.

Maybe someone is going to one shot a viral master piece one day. Or, not one shot but relatively close to it, from someone non technical. I mean, looking at something like Vampire Survivors for example. The idea and technicality isn't really that crazy. But its all the little things that came together to make it satisfying, with an interesting basic premise.

OK you're a painter. An author. Show me the book. Show me the painting.

Its hard to make something good. So many things will get called not-good. Could something "low effort" be good? Potentially. But you shouldn't be surprised if something you made with little effort is criticized as not good.

replies.author: TopTippityTop
replies.body:
Not sure I agree.

Someone who occasionally paints isn't a painter any more than someone who occasionally cooks is a chef, or someome who drove a car in a race track is a race car driver.

That is a profession.

A developer is someone who de votes their life towards developing. A painter does the same for painting. A author for writing.

Publishing a book = author. Not necessarily a good one.

Writing some words down = not really an author, just someone writing.

replies.author: SpiritualShallot3
replies.body: I’d say I disagree personally. Painter, poet, writer, etc are incredibly broad descriptions of pursuits, I don’t think it necessarily implies they do it professionally or even successfully.

comments.author: EnvironmentFirst4839
comments.body: Not a single original thought here, good work!

comments.author: JDad67
comments.body:
Who made GTA 6?   
Rockstar Games. A collection of dedicated employees: Devs, artists, Product managers, Marketers. but the biggest name on the box is the company that paid for all those people. 

How does that change if I make a game and AI is one of the tools I use?

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: People don't seem to understand simple computing evolution where we always move to a higher level of abstraction as time goes by.

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body: Agree, this is very obvious. Same with camera phones and photographers/cinematographers, etc.

comments.author: Exhales_Deeply
comments.body: I think there's a spectrum. And this sub encompasses the entire thing. So you can't be surprised that folks who've never been criticized in their entire creative career (one day) don't know what to make of it

comments.author: sfc1971
comments.body: Anyone can post an opinion on Reddit, it doesn't make them insightful.
